disclosures.said: Some of the pictures have thin dashed outlines drawn in by the camera tool that took them. Disregard those dashed outlines — only the solid coloured boxes with a tag matter.

screen1-a1.where: the three short lines in the top left corner
screen1-a1.expectation: It opens the app's main menu, the list of places I can go.
screen1-a1.cue: The three stacked lines. I have learned that shape means a menu, and it sits where menus usually sit.

first_pass.why: This is one picture I do know by now. I would say 'tap menu' or tap it and expect the side list to open.

screen1-a2.where: the little outlined ghost at the top right
screen1-a2.expectation: I do not know. It is a small ghost face. I cannot connect a ghost to anything I would want to do in a chat app.
screen1-a2.cue: Only the picture of the ghost. There are no words next to it at all.

first_pass.why: I cannot recognise what a ghost is supposed to stand for, and nothing on the screen names it. I would not press it, because I could not predict where it would take me, and I could not ask for it by voice because I do not know what to call it.
first_pass.solution: Put a word under it or beside it that says what it does, in plain terms. If it starts a private chat, say 'Private chat'.

test_cases.targets: whether anything tells you what the ghost does before it changes the screen, or only afterwards
test_cases.action: Start from the main screen (the one with the typing box at the bottom). If you are not there, press the three lines at the top left and then 'New chat'. Hold your finger on the ghost at the top right for about a second and watch for any words. Then read what the screen now says. To go back, press the same corner control again.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: no words name it before anything changes, and you only find out what it did after it has done it
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: words appear (on holding, or near it) that tell you what it does before anything changes
test_cases.what_happened: I held my finger on the ghost at the top right for a second. No words appeared at all: the ghost just got a grey circle behind it, and then the whole screen switched to one headed 'Incognito chat' with the explanation 'Incognito chats stay out of your history and search, and aren't used to train Claude.' So holding it did not tell me anything; it simply did the thing. I only learned what the ghost means after it had already changed my screen. The same corner then showed an X, which took me back.

screen1-a2.closing_comment: I only found out what the ghost does after it had done it; holding it gives no name first, so I still could not predict it or ask for it by voice.

screen1-a3.where: the purple 'Upgrade to Pro' words on the grey strip above the typing box
screen1-a3.expectation: It takes me to a page where I can pay for the Pro version.
screen1-a3.cue: The words 'Upgrade to Pro' and the line beside them, 'Get more with Claude Pro'.

first_pass.why: The words say exactly what will happen.

screen1-a4.where: the long typing box that says 'Chat with Claude...'
screen1-a4.expectation: The question or message I want to send to Claude.
screen1-a4.cue: The grey words 'Chat with Claude...' inside the box.

first_pass.why: It is a plain typing box and the words inside it tell me what it is for.

screen1-a5.where: the round plus button at the bottom left of the typing area
screen1-a5.expectation: It adds something, but I am not sure what: perhaps a file or picture to the message, perhaps a whole new chat.

first_pass.why: A plus means 'add', but add what? It could equally be a new chat or an attachment. I would read the area over and over and still not be able to commit.
first_pass.solution: A short word next to it, such as 'Attach' or 'Add file', so I know which kind of adding it is.

test_cases.targets: which kind of adding the plus does (a file, a new chat, a project)
test_cases.action: Start from the main screen (the one with the typing box at the bottom). If you are not there, press the three lines at the top left and then 'New chat'. Press the plus in the round grey button at the bottom left of the typing bar. Read what opens, without pressing anything inside it. Close it with the X at its top left.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what opens is not what you expected, or it still does not settle which kind of adding it is
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens matches what you expected and makes the plus's job clear
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the round plus. A panel slid up titled 'Add to chat' with Camera, Photos and Files, then 'Add to project', 'Web search', 'Connectors' and 'Memory'. So the plus is about adding things to my message, not starting a new chat. I closed it with the X.

screen1-a5.closing_comment: Now I know the plus means 'add to this chat', and the panel's title says so plainly; but I only know it after pressing it, and nothing next to the plus itself says it.

screen1-a6.where: the grey rounded button with 'Haiku 4.5' on it, next to the plus
screen1-a6.expectation: I am guessing it lets me change some setting or version, because it has a number on it. A haiku is a short poem, so part of me wonders whether it makes Claude write poems.
screen1-a6.cue: The words 'Haiku 4.5'. They are a name, not an instruction.

first_pass.why: The words are there, but they do not say what the button does. 'Haiku' has a meaning I already know, and it is the wrong one here, so I get stuck on the ambiguity.
first_pass.solution: A small label that says what it is, such as 'Model: Haiku 4.5', or a down-arrow so I know it opens a choice.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing the 'Haiku 4.5' pill shows what it is and that it is something you can change
test_cases.action: Start from the main screen (the one with the typing box at the bottom). If you are not there, press the three lines at the top left and then 'New chat'. Press the pill in the typing bar that says 'Haiku 4.5'. Read what opens, without choosing anything. Close it with the X at its top left.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: you still cannot tell what 'Haiku 4.5' is or what changing it would do
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens tells you plainly what the pill is for
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed 'Haiku 4.5'. A panel titled 'Select model' opened with a list of names, each with a short line saying what it is good for, and Haiku 4.5 has a tick. So the pill shows which model is in use and lets me change it. I closed it with the X without choosing.

screen1-a6.closing_comment: 'Select model' made it plain, so it is not about poems; but the pill on the main screen still only shows a name, and I have to remember what it means.

screen1-a7.where: the round grey microphone button, second from the right at the bottom
screen1-a7.expectation: It lets me speak instead of typing, so my words are turned into text.
screen1-a7.cue: The microphone picture. I use speech recognition, so I know that picture well.

first_pass.why: On its own I would be fairly confident. But right next to it is a second button that also looks to do with sound, and I cannot tell which of the two is for dictating and which is for something else. With two voice-looking buttons side by side I lose my certainty.
first_pass.solution: Words under each of the two buttons that make the difference plain, for example 'Dictate' under this one and 'Voice conversation' under the other.

test_cases.targets: telling the microphone apart from the round black button beside it
test_cases.action: Start from the main screen (the one with the typing box at the bottom). If you are not there, press the three lines at the top left and then 'New chat'. Press the microphone (the grey round button, second from the right). Read what appears. Do NOT press Continue. Close it with the X at the top left.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what appears does not help you tell the two round buttons apart
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what appears makes it clear what the microphone does and so how it differs from its neighbour
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the grey microphone. A full page opened: 'Send messages to Claude using your voice.' with 'Choose a language to speak in', 'Speak for up to 10 minutes', a Speech Input Language box set to English, and a Continue button. I did not press Continue; I closed it with the X.

screen1-a7.closing_comment: The microphone is dictation, which is what I thought, so I can now tell it apart from its black neighbour; but the two still look alike and neither has a word under it.

screen1-a8.where: the black filled circle with little vertical lines, at the far bottom right
screen1-a8.expectation: Something with voice or sound. It could be a spoken conversation, or it might be the send button, because the bottom right is where send usually is.
screen1-a8.cue: Only the picture of the vertical lines, like a sound wave, and its position where a send button would normally be.

first_pass.why: I cannot choose between two readings: send my message, or start talking. They are very different actions, and the one next to it also looks like sound. I would hesitate here every time.
first_pass.solution: A word on or under it saying what it does, and keep a separate, clearly named send button.

test_cases.targets: whether the round black button with bars could be the send button, and whether anything tells it apart from the microphone
test_cases.action: Start from the main screen (the one with the typing box at the bottom). If you are not there, press the three lines at the top left and then 'New chat'. Do not press the round black button. Tap the typing box and type the word test (do not send). Watch the round black button while you type, then delete the word and watch again.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: nothing on the screen tells you what the black button is, whether or not you have typed
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: the screen shows you plainly what the black button is for, or which button sends
test_cases.what_happened: I tapped the typing box and typed 'test' without sending. As soon as there were letters, the round black button with bars changed into an orange circle with an up arrow, which is clearly send. When I deleted the word it went back to the black circle with bars. So the black button is not send; send only appears when there is text. Nothing ever named what the black button with bars does.

test_cases.targets: what the round black button actually does when pressed
test_cases.action: (not run) Pressing the round black button itself.
test_cases.what_happened: Not run, as instructed. I did not press the round black button. Not executed: no — this test would start a feature this session does not allow on the phones, so it was not run

screen1-a8.closing_comment: Typing showed me that send is a separate orange arrow, so this is not send; but I never learned what the black button with bars does, and it has no word.

screen2-a1.where: the dimmed grey strip down the right edge, behind the menu
screen2-a1.expectation: I think tapping the grey part closes the menu and takes me back to the screen underneath.
screen2-a1.cue: Nothing written. Only that the screen behind is greyed out and still partly visible.

first_pass.why: There is nothing drawn there to press; I would only know from habit that tapping outside closes a menu. I can also see a bit of the old screen's buttons through the grey, and I would worry I was pressing those instead.
first_pass.solution: A clear close button or a 'Back' word at the top of the menu, so I do not have to guess that the grey area is a button.

test_cases.targets: whether tapping the grey strip does the job of the little picture showing through it, or just closes the menu
test_cases.action: Start from the main screen (the one with the typing box at the bottom). If you are not there, press the three lines at the top left and then 'New chat'. Press the three lines at the top left to open the side menu. Tap the grey strip on the right exactly where the little ghost shows through. Watch what happens.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: the menu closes but the picture you pressed does not do its own job, or you could not tell you were allowed to tap there
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what happens is exactly what you expected from what you could see in the strip
test_cases.what_happened: I opened the side menu and tapped the grey strip exactly where the little ghost shows through. The menu slid closed and I was back on the main screen. The ghost did not do its job; it was not an incognito chat. That is what I had guessed would happen.

screen2-a1.closing_comment: Tapping the grey area just closed the menu, as I guessed, and did not press the ghost behind it; I still had to rely on habit to know I could tap there.

screen2-a2.where: the big word 'Claude' at the top of the menu
screen2-a2.expectation: I do not expect anything. It looks like the name of the app, a title. If it does something, perhaps it takes me home.
screen2-a2.cue: Only the word 'Claude', written like a heading.

first_pass.why: It reads as a title, not a button. I cannot tell that it does anything, and if it does, nothing says what.
first_pass.solution: If it takes me home, say 'Home'. If it does nothing, it should not behave like a button.

test_cases.targets: whether the big word 'Claude' does anything when pressed, and whether you could have guessed it
test_cases.action: Start from the main screen (the one with the typing box at the bottom). If you are not there, press the three lines at the top left and then 'New chat'. Press the three lines at the top left to open the side menu. Press the big word 'Claude' at the top of the menu. Watch what happens.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: it does something the word did not tell you, or you still cannot tell what it did
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: it behaves as you expected (for example nothing happens, or it plainly takes you home)
test_cases.what_happened: I opened the side menu and pressed the big word 'Claude' at the top. The menu closed and I landed on a fresh main screen with the typing box ready and the keyboard up, the same as starting a new chat. So it takes me home.

screen2-a2.closing_comment: It did take me home, which was one of my guesses, so no harm; but the word still looks like a title, not a button, and does not say 'Home'.

screen2-a3.where: the 'Chats' line with the speech-bubble picture, first in the menu
screen2-a3.expectation: It shows me my earlier conversations.
screen2-a3.cue: The word 'Chats' and the two speech bubbles.

first_pass.why: The word is plain and the picture agrees with it.

screen2-a4.where: the 'Projects' line, second in the menu
screen2-a4.expectation: It takes me to a page called Projects, where things are organised into projects.

first_pass.why: I am not certain what a 'project' means in this app, but I am certain where I will end up: a page called Projects. That is enough for me to press it.

screen2-a5.where: the 'Code' line with the angle-bracket picture, third in the menu
screen2-a5.expectation: Something to do with computer programming, perhaps writing code with Claude. It could also mean a code I have to enter, like a verification code.
screen2-a5.cue: The word 'Code' and the </> picture, which I know from my work means programming.

first_pass.why: One short word with two ordinary meanings. The picture tips me towards programming, but I still read it twice to be sure.
first_pass.solution: A few more words, for example 'Code with Claude'.

test_cases.targets: which meaning of 'Code' this is and what you get by pressing it
test_cases.action: Start from the main screen (the one with the typing box at the bottom). If you are not there, press the three lines at the top left and then 'New chat'. Press the three lines at the top left to open the side menu. Press 'Code'. Read the page. If anything asks for payment or a plan change, do not press it. Go back with the three lines at the top left and 'New chat'.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: the page is not what you expected from the word 'Code'
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: the page is what you expected from the word
test_cases.what_happened: I opened the side menu and pressed 'Code'. The page showed an example of a coding conversation ('Make Clawd dance', with file names and code) and underneath 'Upgrade for Claude Code — Your agentic coding partner that works directly in your codebase.' with 'Upgrade' and 'Return to chat' buttons. I did not press Upgrade. It is about computer programming, not a verification code.

screen2-a5.closing_comment: The page is about programming, as the picture suggested, so my doubt was resolved; I would still prefer the menu line to say 'Code with Claude', and it turns out to be an upgrade page rather than a place to work.

screen2-a6.where: the 'Artifacts' line with the circle-and-shapes picture, last in the menu
screen2-a6.expectation: I have no idea. An artifact to me is an old object in a museum. I cannot think what it means in a chat app.
screen2-a6.cue: The word 'Artifacts' and a picture of overlapping shapes, which does not help me.

first_pass.why: The word has a meaning I know, and it clearly is not the meaning here, so I cannot commit to anything. The shapes picture adds nothing I can recognise.
first_pass.solution: Use plain words for what is kept there, or add a short line under it, for example 'Things Claude made for you'.

test_cases.targets: whether you can find out what an 'artifact' is
test_cases.action: Start from the main screen (the one with the typing box at the bottom). If you are not there, press the three lines at the top left and then 'New chat'. Press the three lines at the top left to open the side menu. Press 'Artifacts'. Read everything on the page.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: nothing there tells you in plain words what an artifact is
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: the page tells you plainly what artifacts are
test_cases.what_happened: I opened the side menu and pressed 'Artifacts'. The page title is 'Artifacts', with a search box, an 'All' dropdown, a sliders button, a picture of shapes and one line: 'Artifacts you've had with Claude will show up here.' Nothing on this page says what an artifact is. The only explanation I found was later, by chance, in Settings under Capabilities: 'Generate content like code snippets, text documents, or website designs in a dedicated window.'

screen2-a6.closing_comment: The Artifacts page never says what an artifact is; the only explanation is hidden two screens deep in Settings, where I would never think to look.

screen2-a7.where: the orange circle with 'AC' at the bottom left of the menu
screen2-a7.expectation: My account or profile. AC matches the name in the greeting, Ally Cooper.
screen2-a7.cue: The letters 'AC' and the greeting 'Back at it, Ally Cooper' on the main screen.

first_pass.why: I had to put two things together to work it out: the initials and a name I saw on another screen. Initials alone do not say 'account' or 'settings'.

test_cases.targets: what the AC circle opens
test_cases.action: Start from the main screen (the one with the typing box at the bottom). If you are not there, press the three lines at the top left and then 'New chat'. test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what opens is not what you guessed, or you still would not know next time what the circle is for
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: it opens what you guessed (your account or settings)

screen2-a7.closing_comment: It opens Settings, as I guessed; but I had to piece it together from initials, and a word such as 'Settings' beside the circle would save me that step each time.
